en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River, located in the Cagayan Valley region, is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching for approximately 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers south of Metro Manila.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest underwater trench in the country, plunging to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters below sea level.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, spanning roughly 14,649 square kilometers in the Mimaropa region.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an underground river that flows directly into the sea for about 8.2 kilometers.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon, making it the longest mountain range in the Philippines at 540 kilometers.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is the second-highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,928 meters above sea level and famous for its sea of clouds.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, covering a land area of approximately 109,965 square kilometers.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones or typhoons each year as they pass through the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is one of the most active volcanoes in the country, featuring a main crater that spans about 2 kilometers in diameter.
